 PLEASE NOTE--The numerical order of items on this agenda is for convenience of reference.
Items may be taken out of order upon request of the Mayor or Members of the City Council.
Members of the City Council and the public are reminded that they must preserve order and
decorum throughout the Meeting. In that regard, Members of the City Council and the public
are advised that any delay or disruption in the proceedings or a refusal to obey the orders of
the City Council or the presiding officer constitutes a violation of these rules.

  •  The conduct of City Council meetings is governed by the portion of the California
  Government Code commonly known as the "Brown Act" and by the Huntington Park
  City Council Meeting Rules of Procedure.

  •  The City Council meeting is for conducting the City's business, and members of the
  audience must obey the rules of decorum set forth by law. This means that each
  speaker will be permitted to speak for three minutes to address items that are listed
  on the City Council agenda or topics which are within the jurisdictional authority of the
  City.

  •  No profanity, personal attacks, booing, cheering, applauding or other conduct
  disruptive to the meeting will be permitted. Any person not adhering to the Rules of
  Procedure or conduct authorized by the Brown Act may be asked to leave the Council
  Chambers.

  •  All comments directed to the City Council or to any member of the City Council must
  be directed to the Mayor (or Chairperson if Mayor is absent).

We ask that you please respect the business nature of this meeting and the order required
for the proceedings conducted in the Council Chambers.

PUBLIC COMMENT

For both open and closed session, each speaker will be limited to three minutes per
Huntington Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not be shared with other
speakers and may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another or from one
meeting to another. This is the only opportunity for public input except for scheduled
public hearing items.

All comments or queries shall be addressed to the Council as a body and not to any specific
member thereof. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(a)(2), the Ralph M. Brown
Act, no action or discussion by the City Council shall be undertaken on any item not appearing
on the posted agenda, except to briefly provide information, ask for clarification, provide
direction to staff, or schedule a matter for a future meeting.
ADDITIONS/DELETIONS TO AGENDA

Items of business may be added to the agenda upon a motion adopted by a minimum two-
thirds vote finding that there is a need to take immediate action and that the need for action
came to the attention of the City or Agency subsequent to the agenda being posted. Items
may be deleted from the agenda upon the request of staff or Council.

REGULAR AGENDA

CITY MANAGER

  1. CONSIDERATION OF FILLING VACANT COUNCIL MEMBER POSITION

Per the Municipal Code from the day a vacancy is made on the City Council, the City Council
has 60 days to fill the vacancy.
The City Manager presented the alternatives that Councilmembers could take in regards to
filling vacant council member commissions.
1) By adopting Resolution No. 2025-06.
  1) FIlling Vacancy by Special Election to be held not less than 114 days from the call of
  the special election; or
  2) FIlling Vacancy by appointment until the next regularly scheduled election, scheduled
  to be held on March 3, 2026; or
  3) take necessary related actions that may be desirable.

On February 18, 2025; the position held by Councilmember Esmeralda Castillo was deemed
vacant following an investigation into a complaint received by the City of Huntington Park in
September of 2024. The complaint alleged Councilmember Castillo was not a resident in the
CIty. The investigation confirmed that she did not have residency in the CIty of Huntington Park.
As a result, City Council is obligated in filling the vacancy either by appointment or by special
election.

If the council calls for a special election, the City Council will have to establish a special election
date within 114 days from the call of the special election. The individual elected will hold the
office until the expiration of the term March of 2028. County clerk office has no election
scheduled from now until that date, thus this election can not be consolidated with any other
county, state, or election and would be determined a special election. The election would also
come at the City’s expense which could be upwards of 500,000 dollars. Staff will prepare
resolutions

Or appoint an individual to fill the vacancy until the next general election scheduled for March 3,
2026. City of Huntington Park Municipal Code does not hold a formal process on the
appointment process so council would need to create one. Councilmembers can solicit
applications, and conduct interviews prior to making an appointment. City Council may choose
but is not required to solicit and or conduct interviews prior to making the appointment. If council
chooses to make an appointment, it must be done within 60 days of the vacancy. Since vacancy
was made on February 18, 2025, council members would need to fill vacancy by April 21, 2025
 (since April 18, 2025 falls on a Saturday). Appointees must be a resident in the City of
Huntington Park, must be a registered voter, and must be the age of 18 years old at time of
appointment. If council serves as appointee he would be required to run in the 2026 general
election if interested in retaining his position. If elected in 2026, individuals would serve the
remainder of the term (expires in March 2028).

Investigation Detail Breifing: Council and the Public were briefed with basics regarding the
investigation into Councilmember Castillo’s residency. As it is an active investigation only brief
information was provided. Once completed more information would be granted.

MOTION: Councilmember Sanabria motioned to appoint adopted RESOLUTION 2025-06 and
fill the vacancy by appointment. With a deadline application on Friday, March 28, 2025. Public
candidacy three-minute presentations will be conducted at the regularly scheduled city council
meeting of Monday, April 7, 2025; and, possible appointments being on Monday, April 7, 2025
and/ or guaranteed appointment at a following special or regularly scheduled City Council
Meeting on or before April 21, 2025 (the 60 day deadline) of the individuals who applied and
presented. The motion was then second by Vice Mayor Flores. The motion passed by majority
consent.

AYES: Council Member (s): Martinez, Sanabria, and Vice Mayor Flores

NOES: Council Member (s): Mayor Macias. (Mayor Macias wanted to state that the process is
illegal).

ABSENT: None

None

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

Graciela Carbajal and Denise Romero regarding Item #1.

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Sanabria: Thanks to all staff and community members who came out tonight. Decision to
uphold Municipal Code was why they were elected. Since last time there was a change on
council about ten years ago. Was part of that group who tried to make changes for the
community. He failed to see Rent Stabalization, changing Huntington Park’s status to a
sanctuary city. All we saw was a change in vendors. But the material lives of residents did not
change. He mentioned the aquatics center. He pushed for the palestinian ordinance and the
lobbying ordinance.
 Martinez: Thank you to all the community members who came out. All facts will come out. Time
will rebuild everything, and we’ll have a better understanding of how the city operates and how
they make decisions and how they move forward.

Flores: Thank you Staff.

Macias: Thanks Staff and Directors. Very proud of the work that has been done in the last 12
years. There’s more work to do. Pool project was stalled due to the county measures, and covid.
Resources had to be redistributed from pool projects to keeping individuals alive. Distributing
food distribution, mask distribution, senior income for a year, income for struggling folks, etc.
Getting transportation money for public transit, and street improvement. That work has been
done in the last 10 years, and there’s more work to do. It’s unfortunate what happened here to
Councilmember Castillo, actions were taken that were illegal. She nor any other members of the
council were judges to make this kind of decision of who and who does not live in the city. She
always carries a little constitution book in her purse, and tonight Councilmember Castillo’s
constitutional rights were violated. People have died to fight for these constitutional rights. That
action was wrong and should’ve never been done. There’s always been disagreements but not
to this magnitude. That’s why I voted No. The City was placed on Notice by an attorney and we
should all be worried.

ADJOURNMENT
Mayor Macias adjourned the meeting at 7:54p.m. The next City of Huntington Park City
Council meeting will be held on Monday, March 3, 2025 at 6:00 pm.

Respectfully submitted

Eduardo Sarmiento, City Clerk
